step_by_step_reasoning: The visual architecture shows CloudHealth SecureState's real-time cloud security ingestion and evaluation engine. Nodes were mapped strictly to the valid vocabulary: Kinesis Data Streams (Collect), Kinesis Data Streams (Rules), Neptune (graph database), Elasticsearch (mapped to OpenSearch per AWS service guidelines), CloudWatch (monitoring), DynamoDB (persistence), and ThirdParty Notifications (Slack, email, Splunk). Edge flows were identified across three main logical stages: 1) Data collection and persistence to Neptune, Elasticsearch, and DynamoDB; 2) Monitoring and sharding feedback loop leveraging CloudWatch metrics to balance write scaling into Neptune; 3) Rule execution pipeline querying Neptune for graph checks, persisting violations to DynamoDB, and pushing notifications to external channels.

nodes.name: Kinesis Data Streams (Collect)
nodes.notes: Ingests real-time cloud security events and evaluates resource state from cloud providers.

nodes.name: Kinesis Data Streams (Rules)
nodes.notes: Buffers incoming events and resource changes for the security rule execution engine.

nodes.name: Neptune
nodes.notes: Primary schema-less graph database storing 50M+ interconnected cloud resources for topology exploration and rule queries.

nodes.name: Elasticsearch
nodes.notes: Backing store powering search aggregations, reporting, analytics, and historical configuration tracking.

nodes.name: CloudWatch
nodes.notes: Monitors CPU, memory, and performance metrics from Neptune and Elasticsearch to inform the Sharder service.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Backing store persisting resource configurations and detected security violations.

nodes.name: Notifications
nodes.notes: External notification channels including Slack, email, and Splunk for real-time risk alerts.
